sections.description: REST working surface for bethanycentral.org: site introspection, arbitrary post meta, and The Events Calendar recurring events including "will not occur" exclusion dates — none of which core or plugin REST APIs expose — REST-managed path redirects, plus the site's custom PHP tweaks, updated through this plugin instead of hand-edited snippets.
sections.changelog:
0.12.0

  • New files module — the SFTP replacement, fenced to wp-content/mu-plugins and the active child theme: GET /files/{root}, GET/PUT/DELETE /files/{root}/{path}, POST /files/restore. Content travels base64 (the host firewall 403s PHP in request bodies). Every .php write is syntax-checked first (php -l via exec, else opcache_compile_file()), functions that would redeclare an existing runtime function are refused without force, overwrites require the current expected_sha1, the previous version is copied to wp-content/bsb-backups/<random>/ (never inside an auto-loaded dir) and can be restored. Writes are atomic (write-beside + rename) and invalidate OPcache.

0.11.0

  • New content module: GET /content/find searches post content, post meta and options (core search only sees post content; Cornerstone's JSON-escaped slashes are matched too) and POST /content/replace rewrites them serialized-safely with a dry run that is the exact plan.
  • PUT /events/{ref}: edit an event's ordinary fields through tribe_update_event() with only the fields passed — TEC's own REST wipes what it isn't told about. Recurrence is snapshotted and restored, occurrence counts compared, and dates on a recurring series require apply_to=series + expected_count.
  • Redirects: per-rule hit counts and referers (persisted at most every 10 minutes per path), and a nested-404 rescue — a multi-segment 404 whose last segment is exactly one published page or post's slug is 301'd to it and logged, so the moved-parent case fixes itself. Off via option bsb_redirects_settings {"rescue":false}.

0.10.0

  • New options module: GET /options?search=, GET/PUT/DELETE /options/{name} — wp_options read/written like /meta, with a blocklist for site-critical options and a refusal to read or write credential-looking names.
  • POST /site/update-plugin: install an update WordPress is already offering (defaults to this plugin) via Plugin_Upgrader::bulk_upgrade(), the same path as wp-admin's Update now. Removes the last manual click from a release.
  • POST /site/purge-cache: clear Hummingbird page cache, the hosting static server cache where a purge method is present, the object cache and OPcache; reports each layer as cleared/unavailable, probe=1 lists what is there.
  • POST /site/flush-rewrites: the Permalinks → Save step.
  • Fix: PUT /meta stripped backslashes — update_post_meta() expects slashed input and REST JSON is unslashed, so Cornerstone's JSON-in-a-string meta landed corrupted. Values are now wp_slash()ed first.
  • GET /site capabilities now report hummingbird_page_cache, opcache, object_cache.

0.9.3

  • New redirects module: path → URL redirects managed over REST (GET/PUT/DELETE /redirects), served on template_redirect. Added because /contact/email-preferences died when the Contact page moved under About — WordPress's own 404 guess rescues a bare /contact/ but never a nested child path, and nothing on the site could add that redirect over REST (the Pretty Links bridge sanitizes slashes out of slugs; Quick Page/Post Redirect is wp-admin only). Exact rules and /* prefix rules (with * in to to carry the remainder); query strings ride along; self-redirects are refused; writes are DB-verified and report the page a rule would shadow. GET /site now lists redirects in modules and reports bridge.redirect_rules.

0.9.2

  • Fix: the token saved via PUT /site/gf-poke-token never persisted — update_option() reported success while the host's persistent object cache kept serving the stale "option does not exist" (notoptions) entry planted by earlier reads. Option writes are now verified against the database row directly (with a raw upsert fallback) and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of claiming success; reads fall back to the database and heal the cache. Also applied to the rewrite-flush guard, which was otherwise flushing rewrite rules on every request.

0.9.1

  • The GF poke token can now be stored as a WP option via authenticated PUT /site/gf-poke-token (confirm=true; the token is never echoed back) — for hosts with no file access. Added because the site's Theme File Editor can't save: its loopback fatal-check is blocked by the firewall in front of the site. The ATLAS_GF_POKE_TOKEN constant still wins when defined.
  • GET /site reports bridge.gf_poke_token as constant / option / null — the token's source, never its value.

0.9.0

  • New tweaks module: the site's custom PHP, absorbed from the Code Snippets plugin so changes ship as a git commit + one-click update instead of hand-edits in wp-admin — trip-update nested URLs (was snippet #5), trip breadcrumbs (#6), the [ff_date] shortcode (#7), and the Gravity Forms → Atlas poke (#8).
  • The GF poke now posts to atlas.bethanycentral.org and reads its token from a new ATLAS_GF_POKE_TOKEN constant in wp-config.php — the value stays out of this public repo. Until the constant is defined the poke is skipped (an admin notice says so) and the GF → Sheets sync falls back to its daily cron.
  • Every absorbed function is function_exists()-guarded, so the plugin and the old snippets can safely overlap during cutover. After updating: add the constant, test a form submission, then deactivate snippets #5–#8.
  • One-time rewrite-rules flush replaces the "Permalinks > Save" step the trip-update snippet needed.

0.8.1

  • New POST /site/check-updates: forces core's plugin update check so the "Update now" link actually appears. Two caches decide that — this plugin's manifest cache (which ?refresh_update=1 busts, and which only affects what /site reports) and core's update_plugins transient, refreshed by WP-Cron roughly every 12h. After 0.8.0 the first was fresh and the second stale, so /site reported an update while wp-admin offered none. This drops both, runs the check synchronously, and reports whether the update is now being offered, already current, or the plugin is untracked entirely.

0.8.0

  • Fix: events created through POST /events had no "Register Now" button. The theme gates that button on the ACF field use_event_url_for_registration, not on _EventURL. That field defaults to on, but an ACF default is only applied on an ACF save and tribe_create_event() bypasses ACF entirely — so it landed unset rather than defaulted.
  • ACF field-group defaults for tribe_events are now applied on create, read from ACF's own field groups rather than a hardcoded list, so a field added to the group later is picked up with no plugin change. Existing values are never overwritten.
  • New optional acf parameter to override a default on create, and apply_acf_defaults=false to opt out. The response echoes the values read back off the saved post.
  • Fills in TEC's currency meta (_EventCurrencyCode / _EventCurrencySymbol / _EventCurrencyPosition), skipped on the same path.

0.7.1

  • Fix: wp-admin said "Auto-updates are not available for this plugin". Core skips an Update URI plugin that reports no pending update, so it landed in neither the response nor no_update bucket of the update transient and WP concluded updates weren't supported. The plugin now registers its own no_update entry, so the Enable auto-updates toggle appears.

0.7.0

  • One-click updates from this repo (no more zip uploads).
  • Fix: event category and tags were silently dropped on create — tribe_create_event() ignores tax_input. Terms are now set explicitly and echoed back from the saved post.
  • New featured_media parameter on event create.
  • GET /site now reports installed vs latest version.

0.6.0

  • Per-date times on additional-date rules; count the series start as its own occurrence.

0.5.0

  • Wait for TEC to finish regenerating occurrences before reporting, so a successful write can no longer report itself as failed.

0.4.0

  • Recurrence array shape calibrated against the live site.

0.3.0

  • Renamed to Bethany Site Bridge; added the site and meta modules.
